EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2880, 2937 and 2980 cm⁻¹, together with CH₂/CH₃ deformation bands at 1458 and 1491 cm⁻¹ and wag/twist bands at 1277, 1121 and 1066 cm⁻¹ – a pattern typical of a straight-chain saturated/weakly unsaturated hydrocarbon. Peaks at 2812 cm⁻¹ are consistent with the Fermi-resonance aldehydic C–H stretch (≈ 2820 cm⁻¹), and the absence of a prominent Raman carbonyl band is expected because C=O stretches are usually weak in Raman. Among the candidates the only structures consistent with (i) prominent aliphatic C–H features, (ii) an aldehydic C–H stretch near 2820 cm⁻¹, and (iii) no other strong hetero-atom stretches in the observed region are the linear alkanals 1 (heptanal, CCCCCCC=O) and 3 (hexanal, CCCCCC=O). The spectra of these two compounds are extremely similar; choosing the top-ranked candidate, heptanal (1), best matches the observed pattern while respecting retrieval ordering.
